chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 2 of 21), named for no shrine: most confess the poet's bondage to women and their embraces and ask for the feet, two face the funeral pyre and Death's messengers, one sets the Lord's form beyond what all the sects and scriptures know, and one appears to give the lovesickness of women who watch the god pass in the street; the praise leans heavily on Vishnu's avatars as Murugan's uncle and on the ghouls feasting on the battlefield.
structure_note: Courtesan and lovemaking songs (1007 to 1010, 1012, 1015, 1017 to 1020); the body and the pyre (1014, 1019, 1021); the scriptures' limits (1011, 1016); a love-lament probably in another voice (1013). Songs 1012 to 1015 and 1018 to 1021 are in markedly harder, denser rhythms.

1007.reading: After a frank picture of lovemaking with women who swear 'you are my very life', the poet does not ask to be pulled out: he vows that whether he sinks, rises or tosses in that ocean of passion he will never forget to think and say that Murugan's two feet are his life's help. The praise shows the battlefield of vultures, ghouls and dancing Bhairavi, Rama's one arrow felling the ten crowns and twenty arms, and Murugan, nephew of that Vishnu, the guru and Saravana who rides the peacock so that Indra regains his city.
1007.nuance: அநுராக உததியதனிடை விழுகினும் எழுகினும் உழலுகினும் உனது அடியிணை எனது உயிர் உதவி என ... மறவேனே: the song ends its plea with a vow (மறவேனே) rather than a request, setting remembrance of the feet inside the passion instead of after escape from it.

1008.reading: The poet describes women whose eyes are spears and whose music oozes blame, who strike young men without pause like Death himself with his net of karma's darkness, and asks not to capsize in the shoreless sea of fate through infatuation with them, but to have the lotus feet of the Kumara who melted for the hunter girl in mind even in dreams. The praise names Vishnu who sleeps on the serpent and measured the earth, Murugan the great one who told Siva on the bull 'this is the supreme knowledge', and the vel that turned the asuras' chests to mire.
1008.nuance: இடைவிடாது எறு நடுவனும் என: the women are likened to நடுவன், Yama, the impartial killer, so desire and death are one figure. கரையிலா விதி எனும் ஒரு கடல்: fate is a sea without shore. The line about learning and knowledge that sages despise (கலைகளும் அறிவொடு கருதொணாதென முனிவுற) is hard to construe.

1009.reading: Infatuated by women's hair, waist, gait, eyes, speech and breasts as by a deadly poison, the poet calls himself a fool falling into hell, a thief who never worshipped, a deceiver and a sinner sunk in lying talk, and asks to be shown one way to reach the lotus feet. The praise is almost wholly of Vishnu: dancer on the serpent's head, measurer of the worlds, splitter of Hiranya, Rama of the single arrow, Krishna who fought the marutha trees and played the flute to the cattle; Murugan is his nephew and the lover of the dark hunters' girl.
1009.nuance: The self-abuse is a pileup of rhymed nouns (அவலனை, அசடனை, திருடனை, மருடனை, கபடனை, விகடனை), its rhythm part of the confession. The praise spends nearly all its length on Vishnu's avatars before naming Murugan in the last line.

1010.reading: The poet confesses playing day and night with women whose breasts imprison the hearts of a crore of young men, drinking their lips as nectar and sinking in a sea of infatuation, and asks whether there will be a day when he forgets that ruinous karma and lives thinking of the long flower feet. The praise shows the gods and sages hailing Murugan as the demons die, and the ghouls on mountains of fat tasting the flesh, 'this is astringent, this sour, this rotten, this good', and eating until their hunger ends; he is Ganga's son, the hunter girl's husband, the vel that pierced the mountain.
1010.nuance: The ghouls' tasting talk (துவரிது புளியிது தொய்ந்ததீதிது ... உளதென) is a comic set piece inside the battle scene, not stock drum syllables. பகிரதி சிறுவ names Murugan as Ganga's child.

1011.reading: The poet asks when, hearing what the rival sects call the ultimate (form, the formless, a light that is neither, space, heaven, the pillar holding the worlds) and seeing the reality itself, he will rest in awareness and silence, strive for the highest state, not be bewildered by the pleasures of touch, sight, smell and sound, and be freed from the pit of deceitful women into which he, guilty of the five great sins, has fallen. The praise shows the gods crying 'Hara Hara, Siva's son Skanda, refuge!' and Murugan saying 'fear not', the vel that tore the asura's chest, the emerald peacock, and Brahma, Vishnu and Siva praising him.
1011.nuance: உரைதரு பரசமயங்கள் ஓதுவது ... அது பொருள் கண்டு மோனமொடு உணர்வுற: the definitions of the other sects are listed, then passed beyond by seeing the thing itself in silence. Whether the definitions are rejected or taken as partial pointers depends on the syntax, which is unclear. பஞ்ச பாதகன்: the five great sins.

1012.reading: The poet likens women's eyes to the poison that rose when the gods churned the sea with the mountain and the serpent rope, eyes that outdo Kama's five arrows, and asks whether, his mind no longer fixed and faltering on their breasts and troubled in their lies, he will not be given Murugan's red feet like a hundred-petalled lotus. The praise tells of Rama crossing the bridged sea with the monkey army and felling the ten heads and twenty arms, Siva wearing konrai, thumbai, moon and Ganga with the goddess at his side, and Murugan following the parrot-like hunter girl.
1012.nuance: இமையவர் பற்றிக் கடைந்த அன்றெழு நஞ்சுபோலே: the eyes are the halahala poison of the churning, an image that makes the woman's glance as world-threatening as the poison Siva had to swallow.

1013.reading: Women brighten their faces, loose and refill their hair with flowers, adjust their dress and come out through the street courtyards in a line with knowing smiles; then Kama stands, the white crescent burns like the undersea fire, the bees hum and the Malaya breeze wounds the body, and the song asks whether the mind should melt and be troubled by this infatuation. The praise shows the peacock's flight splitting the sky and whirling Mandara, Murugan dear to the three-eyed Self-born, victor of the hunters' war, and the child whom Sankari Gauri took up and fed from her breast.
1013.nuance: The plea has no first person. The women dressing and coming into the street, then afflicted by Kama, the moon, bees and the south wind, look like the ula convention of women who fall in love watching the god's procession; if so the song is in their voice or about them, not the poet's confession. This is an inference from the imagery.

1014.reading: The poet pictures kin wailing at his side, the body on the palm-wood pyre with drums beating, and Death with fire-spitting eyes tying the life tight to take it, and asks that before then he be given to learn, entering their discipline, with the understanding of those who think of Murugan as the giver of the goal. The praise names the vel that pierced the northern mountain, dried the sea and struck down the mango, the teacher of the meaning to Siva of the moon and Ganga, and the Lord of the eternal pure ones who hold fast to the silence that endures when the ages end.
1014.nuance: கதிதரு முருகனும் என நினைபவர் கற்பிற் புக்கு அறிவு ஒக்கக் கற்பது: the remedy for death is to learn in the company and discipline of those who know Murugan as the goal; கற்பு here seems to mean their way or learning, not chastity, but the line is compressed. மவுனத்திற் பற்றுறு நித்தச் சுத்தர்கள்: silence as the refuge of the pure.

1015.reading: The poet, ruined alone by passion for women who flatter a man's skill and melt in many-sided union, asks whether, when Death's host binds him tight and drags him off to hell, the fragrant holy feet, the eternal reality that is release, will not come. The praise tells of Rama's arrow scattering Ravana's twenty arms and golden heads, Murugan who takes Valli with her green parrot, and the vel that shattered Sura's crown while the Bhairavas danced.
1015.nuance: திருவடி முத்திக்குட்படு நித்யத் தத்துவம்: the feet are named as the eternal tattva within release itself. இயல் சிறு வினைமகள் and the vocative இந்த்ரலோகா are unclear: the first seems to be Valli, the second may make Murugan lord of Indra's heaven.

1016.reading: The poet lists who and what cannot know the Lord: the nine siddhas in their caves, Brahma, the asura lords, Siva who burned the cities, Vishnu, Indra with the thunderbolt, the codes of dharma, the Puranas, all the arts and the many Vedas; and asks when, knowing that the Lord's holy form is the knowledge beyond both knowing and not knowing, he will reach the red lotus feet. The praise tells of Vinayaka who, as Vyasa dictated, wrote the Bharata war on the mountain with his broken tusk, the coral elephant after whom Murugan came, and his union with Devayanai.
1016.nuance: அறிவும் அறியாமையும் கடந்த அறிவு திருமேனி: the form of the Lord is itself a knowledge beyond the pair of knowing and ignorance. The myth of Ganesha writing the Mahabharata with his tusk at Vyasa's dictation is named outright (பழுதற வியாசன் அன்று இயம்ப எழுதிய விநாயகன்), with Murugan as his younger brother.

1017.reading: The poet describes lovemaking in detail, hair loosened, face sweating, breasts shaking, the self lost in union, and the love-arts learned from the books of passion, and asks whether he may waste away wandering with young women. The praise shows Murugan going to Sura's battlefield and taking the peacock from his enemy, then going to the hill, bowing even at the hunter girl's feet, wandering unseen by the hunters in the millet field, resolving even to mount the palmyra-stem horse, and at last uniting with her.
1017.nuance: மதனகலை ஆகமங்கள்: the poet calls the manuals of love 'agamas', a mocking echo of scripture. In the praise the god himself takes on the lover's humiliations of Tamil akam poetry: bowing at the girl's feet and resolving to ride the madal (புதிய மடல் ஏறவும் துணிந்த அரிய பரிதாபம்).

1018.reading: The poet confesses becoming the slave of women who stray from the learned path, show sweet talk, musk-smeared breasts, eyes, hair and arms, ask for coins through a broker and stand in the street like peacocks, and asks whether he will cast off that long desire and, going with the devotees, melt and praise and bow at the feet. The praise recalls the churning, Siva who bent the mountain into a bow and smiled the cities into flame and called Murugan the guru of the true meaning, and Murugan, who melted at the speech of the golden myna guarding the millet on the hill.
1018.nuance: தரகொடு கைக்காசைக் கேட்டு: a broker (தரகு) negotiates the price, an unusually concrete detail of the trade. தத்வார்த்தக் குருபரன் என ஓதும்: Siva himself names Murugan guru. The opening lines of the praise (மைச்சாவிக் காக்கைக் கடவுளை ...) are obscure.

1019.reading: The poet tells of a life spent: sent on small errands by sly-eyed women and robbed by them in youth, then bound by the rope of kin and parents and stumbling in bodily toil, then coughing, spitting and losing breath, the body burned in fire, and asks whether there will be a day he escapes this forest of a body. The praise names Murugan the son of the peacock of Kamakottam who gives her breast milk, nephew of Krishna who danced for the cowherd women's curds and milk, the one who came alone on the road so the learned could hear, and the giver of the meaning to Siva who burned Kama.
1019.nuance: The plea moves through three stages of life (சிறுகாலை, the rope of kin, the cough and the pyre), a compressed biography. மெய்க்காடு: the body as a wilderness. காமக் கோட்டக் குலமயில் points to the goddess of Kamakottam at Kanchi. கற்றாவிற் காட்டி ... நற்றாயிற் காட்டி is hard to construe.

1020.reading: The poet describes women who dress their hair, roll their eyes, half-hide their breasts, call, catch and smile, praise a man for money and make love in elaborate postures, and asks Murugan to bear with him who wallowed in that worm-hole of infatuation, call him out at once and protect him. The praise shows the sinner Sura who mocked the Rudras, burst the mountains, sent the gods fleeing and shook the three worlds, and the Kumara whose spear revelled in the sea of his blood.
1020.nuance: பொருட்கு மிகத் துதித்து: the praise is for money. மோகப் புழுத்தொளை, the worm-hole of passion, is among the harshest images for the courtesan. பொறுத்தருளி ... அப்புறத்தில் அழைத்து: the plea is for forbearance and to be called out, not for knowledge.

1021.reading: The poet asks Murugan not to leave him in this body, a hut that houses his heap of karma and the fruit of maya, unable to seek the truth, nor wearied by men who boast 'who can match me, who is so able?' and slight him, but in his grace to set him where he may reach the lotus feet with the taste of Tamil and end death. The praise shows the vel opening a sea of blood from Sura's head, arms and chest, and Murugan joyfully marrying the prattling cuckoo Valli in the hunters' town where she sang in the millet field.
1021.nuance: தமிழ்ச்சுவையிட்டு இறப்பற எய்த்திட: Tamil song is the means of reaching the feet. The first quatrain (இசைக்கும் இடற் குடில், விளைப்பகுதிப் பயப்பளவுற்று) is very compressed and its split into words is a guess.

source_issues: 1010, 1013, 1019: the glyph ஡ stands for ஊ (இலங்கலூடுறு, முன்றிலூடே, தூர்த்த/றூர்த்த).
1007, 1010, 1011, 1019, 1020: initial உ is split from its word by a space (உ ததி, உ ழலுகினும், உ ளதென, உ ரைதரு, உ ற்றார், உ க்காரித்து, உ ருத்திரரை, உ டுத்த).
1011: இருந்ந நாளும probably for இருந்த நாளும.
